Fri

Jul 24OUTBOUND DAYMedium-low confidenceJul 24 · 06:00–22:00 ET
METAR
METAR — the routine surface observation issued hourly by the reporting station, with SPECI reports off-cycle, carrying ceiling, visibility, wind, temperature and altimeter. Issued by the observing station and distributed by aviationweather.gov. This is measured fact, not a forecast, and on this page it describes conditions right now, not this day. A current KLZU observation was read this run. It describes conditions now, not this trip day.
TAF
TAF — the Terminal Aerodrome Forecast, the highest-resolution aviation forecast available. The National Weather Service issues it four times a day, valid 24 to 30 hours, with explicit FM and TEMPO change groups. KLZU has no TAF station, so KPDK is used as a proxy. It is the strongest flight-category evidence this page can show. A KPDK proxy TAF group covers part of this day.
NWS-hr
NWS hourly gridpoint forecast — the National Weather Service digital forecast for the grid cell containing KLZU, updated through the day and reaching about 156 hours. It gives hour-by-hour sky, wind and precipitation probability, and it is the spine of the change windows on this board. The NWS hourly gridpoint forecast reaches this day.
NWS-day
NWS day/night outlook — the same National Weather Service grid summarised into day and night halves, reaching about 168 hours. Coarser than the hourly product but it covers one day further, so this page uses it only to describe spans the hourly forecast cannot reach. Not needed: this day is already covered by the finer-resolution hourly gridpoint forecast.
MAV
GFS MOS (MAV) — Model Output Statistics, the GFS model bias-corrected against decades of observations at this station. Issued by the National Weather Service four times a day in three-hourly steps out to about 72 hours. It carries an explicit ceiling and visibility category, so this page uses it to corroborate the flight category. Beyond the GFS MAV MOS horizon of about 72 hours, or no MAV row carried both a ceiling and a visibility for this day.
MEX
GFS extended MOS (MEX) — the extended-range MOS product, issued twice a day in twelve-hourly steps out to about 192 hours. Coarse, but the only station-calibrated numeric guidance that reaches the far end of a long weekend. This page shows it only as a flagged outlook and never promotes it into a short-range category. This day is already covered by finer-resolution sources.
GFA
GFA and prog charts — the Graphical Forecast for Aviation and the Weather Prediction Center surface progs, issued by the National Weather Service through the day; the surface prog series reaches 144 hours. They are raster images a pilot reads for fronts, pressure systems and precipitation shields. This page displays them with their issuing office and valid time and never interprets them: no category, wind, ceiling, ranking or go/no-go here is derived from an image. The prog-chart panel is built for issue #41 item A-4 but KLZU_PROGCHART_ENABLED is off for this run, so no chart was requested. Grey means not enabled here; it never means clear weather.
NOTAM
FAA NOTAM (NMS) — Notices to Air Missions: closures, outages, obstacles and TFRs, issued continuously by the FAA and valid until cancelled. On this page they are advisory evidence about the airport, not weather, and they never change a flight category. The FAA NMS adapter is built but not enabled on this page. Grey means not enabled here; it never means there are no NOTAMs.

KPDK TAF proxy · regional guidance for KLZU; verify local conditions.

Forecast evidence
METAR
METAR — the routine surface observation issued hourly by the reporting station, with SPECI reports off-cycle, carrying ceiling, visibility, wind, temperature and altimeter. Issued by the observing station and distributed by aviationweather.gov. This is measured fact, not a forecast, and on this page it describes conditions right now, not this day. No usable current THIS AIRPORT observation was available this run (state: unavailable). That says nothing about the forecast for this day.
TAF
TAF — the Terminal Aerodrome Forecast, the highest-resolution aviation forecast available. The National Weather Service issues it four times a day, valid 24 to 30 hours, with explicit FM and TEMPO change groups. Airports without their own TAF station use a nearby proxy, which is a normal condition and not a fault. No usable TAF covers the planned dates at this airport (state: unavailable). A TAF reaches only about 30 hours, so a later trip day being uncovered is a horizon fact, not a fault.
MAV
GFS MOS (MAV) — Model Output Statistics, the GFS model bias-corrected against decades of observations at this station. Issued four times a day in three-hourly steps out to about 72 hours. It carries an explicit ceiling and visibility category, so this card uses it to resolve a day the TAF cannot reach. No usable GFS MOS guidance for the planned dates at this airport (state: unavailable). The product reaches about 72 hours.
MEX
GFS extended MOS (MEX) — the extended-range MOS product, issued twice a day in twelve-hourly steps out to about 192 hours. Coarse, but the only station-calibrated numeric guidance that reaches the far end of a long weekend. This card shows it only as a labelled rough outlook and never as a resolved forecast. No usable MEX MOS guidance for the planned dates at this airport (state: unavailable). The product reaches about 192 hours.
GFA
GFA and prog charts — the Graphical Forecast for Aviation and the Weather Prediction Center surface progs, issued by the National Weather Service through the day; the surface prog series reaches 144 hours. They are raster images a pilot reads for fronts, pressure systems and precipitation shields. This page displays them with their issuing office and valid time and never interprets them: no category, wind, ceiling, ranking or go/no-go here is derived from an image. The prog-chart panel is built for issue #41 item A-4 but KLZU_PROGCHART_ENABLED is off for this run, so no chart was requested. Grey means not enabled here; it never means clear weather.
NOTAM
FAA NOTAM (NMS) — Notices to Air Missions: closures, outages, obstacles and TFRs, issued continuously by the FAA and valid until cancelled. On this page they are advisory evidence about the airport, not weather, and they never change a flight category. The FAA NMS adapter is built but not enabled on this page. Grey means not enabled here; it never means there are no NOTAMs.

A raster chart may be displayed with its issuing office and valid time. No category, wind, ceiling, ranking or go/no-go on this page is derived from, or attributed to, an image. If retrieval fails the slot says UNAVAILABLE; it is never left blank.

Forecast evidence
METAR
METAR — the routine surface observation issued hourly by the reporting station, with SPECI reports off-cycle, carrying ceiling, visibility, wind, temperature and altimeter. Issued by the observing station and distributed by aviationweather.gov. This is measured fact, not a forecast, and on this page it describes conditions right now, not this day. No usable current THIS AIRPORT observation was available this run (state: unavailable). That says nothing about the forecast for this day.
TAF
TAF — the Terminal Aerodrome Forecast, the highest-resolution aviation forecast available. The National Weather Service issues it four times a day, valid 24 to 30 hours, with explicit FM and TEMPO change groups. Airports without their own TAF station use a nearby proxy, which is a normal condition and not a fault. No usable TAF covers the planned dates at this airport (state: unavailable). A TAF reaches only about 30 hours, so a later trip day being uncovered is a horizon fact, not a fault.
MAV
GFS MOS (MAV) — Model Output Statistics, the GFS model bias-corrected against decades of observations at this station. Issued four times a day in three-hourly steps out to about 72 hours. It carries an explicit ceiling and visibility category, so this card uses it to resolve a day the TAF cannot reach. No usable GFS MOS guidance for the planned dates at this airport (state: unavailable). The product reaches about 72 hours.
MEX
GFS extended MOS (MEX) — the extended-range MOS product, issued twice a day in twelve-hourly steps out to about 192 hours. Coarse, but the only station-calibrated numeric guidance that reaches the far end of a long weekend. This card shows it only as a labelled rough outlook and never as a resolved forecast. No usable MEX MOS guidance for the planned dates at this airport (state: unavailable). The product reaches about 192 hours.
GFA
GFA and prog charts — the Graphical Forecast for Aviation and the Weather Prediction Center surface progs, issued by the National Weather Service through the day; the surface prog series reaches 144 hours. They are raster images a pilot reads for fronts, pressure systems and precipitation shields. This page displays them with their issuing office and valid time and never interprets them: no category, wind, ceiling, ranking or go/no-go here is derived from an image. The prog-chart panel is built for issue #41 item A-4 but KLZU_PROGCHART_ENABLED is off for this run, so no chart was requested. Grey means not enabled here; it never means clear weather.
NOTAM
FAA NOTAM (NMS) — Notices to Air Missions: closures, outages, obstacles and TFRs, issued continuously by the FAA and valid until cancelled. On this page they are advisory evidence about the airport, not weather, and they never change a flight category. The FAA NMS adapter is built but not enabled on this page. Grey means not enabled here; it never means there are no NOTAMs.

A raster chart may be displayed with its issuing office and valid time. No category, wind, ceiling, ranking or go/no-go on this page is derived from, or attributed to, an image. If retrieval fails the slot says UNAVAILABLE; it is never left blank.

Forecast evidence
METAR
METAR — the routine surface observation issued hourly by the reporting station, with SPECI reports off-cycle, carrying ceiling, visibility, wind, temperature and altimeter. Issued by the observing station and distributed by aviationweather.gov. This is measured fact, not a forecast, and on this page it describes conditions right now, not this day. No usable current THIS AIRPORT observation was available this run (state: unavailable). That says nothing about the forecast for this day.
TAF
TAF — the Terminal Aerodrome Forecast, the highest-resolution aviation forecast available. The National Weather Service issues it four times a day, valid 24 to 30 hours, with explicit FM and TEMPO change groups. Airports without their own TAF station use a nearby proxy, which is a normal condition and not a fault. No usable TAF covers the planned dates at this airport (state: unavailable). A TAF reaches only about 30 hours, so a later trip day being uncovered is a horizon fact, not a fault.
MAV
GFS MOS (MAV) — Model Output Statistics, the GFS model bias-corrected against decades of observations at this station. Issued four times a day in three-hourly steps out to about 72 hours. It carries an explicit ceiling and visibility category, so this card uses it to resolve a day the TAF cannot reach. No usable GFS MOS guidance for the planned dates at this airport (state: unavailable). The product reaches about 72 hours.
MEX
GFS extended MOS (MEX) — the extended-range MOS product, issued twice a day in twelve-hourly steps out to about 192 hours. Coarse, but the only station-calibrated numeric guidance that reaches the far end of a long weekend. This card shows it only as a labelled rough outlook and never as a resolved forecast. No usable MEX MOS guidance for the planned dates at this airport (state: unavailable). The product reaches about 192 hours.
GFA
GFA and prog charts — the Graphical Forecast for Aviation and the Weather Prediction Center surface progs, issued by the National Weather Service through the day; the surface prog series reaches 144 hours. They are raster images a pilot reads for fronts, pressure systems and precipitation shields. This page displays them with their issuing office and valid time and never interprets them: no category, wind, ceiling, ranking or go/no-go here is derived from an image. The prog-chart panel is built for issue #41 item A-4 but KLZU_PROGCHART_ENABLED is off for this run, so no chart was requested. Grey means not enabled here; it never means clear weather.
NOTAM
FAA NOTAM (NMS) — Notices to Air Missions: closures, outages, obstacles and TFRs, issued continuously by the FAA and valid until cancelled. On this page they are advisory evidence about the airport, not weather, and they never change a flight category. The FAA NMS adapter is built but not enabled on this page. Grey means not enabled here; it never means there are no NOTAMs.

A raster chart may be displayed with its issuing office and valid time. No category, wind, ceiling, ranking or go/no-go on this page is derived from, or attributed to, an image. If retrieval fails the slot says UNAVAILABLE; it is never left blank.

Forecast evidence
METAR
METAR — the routine surface observation issued hourly by the reporting station, with SPECI reports off-cycle, carrying ceiling, visibility, wind, temperature and altimeter. Issued by the observing station and distributed by aviationweather.gov. This is measured fact, not a forecast, and on this page it describes conditions right now, not this day. No usable current THIS AIRPORT observation was available this run (state: unavailable). That says nothing about the forecast for this day.
TAF
TAF — the Terminal Aerodrome Forecast, the highest-resolution aviation forecast available. The National Weather Service issues it four times a day, valid 24 to 30 hours, with explicit FM and TEMPO change groups. Airports without their own TAF station use a nearby proxy, which is a normal condition and not a fault. No usable TAF covers the planned dates at this airport (state: unavailable). A TAF reaches only about 30 hours, so a later trip day being uncovered is a horizon fact, not a fault.
MAV
GFS MOS (MAV) — Model Output Statistics, the GFS model bias-corrected against decades of observations at this station. Issued four times a day in three-hourly steps out to about 72 hours. It carries an explicit ceiling and visibility category, so this card uses it to resolve a day the TAF cannot reach. No usable GFS MOS guidance for the planned dates at this airport (state: unavailable). The product reaches about 72 hours.
MEX
GFS extended MOS (MEX) — the extended-range MOS product, issued twice a day in twelve-hourly steps out to about 192 hours. Coarse, but the only station-calibrated numeric guidance that reaches the far end of a long weekend. This card shows it only as a labelled rough outlook and never as a resolved forecast. No usable MEX MOS guidance for the planned dates at this airport (state: unavailable). The product reaches about 192 hours.
GFA
GFA and prog charts — the Graphical Forecast for Aviation and the Weather Prediction Center surface progs, issued by the National Weather Service through the day; the surface prog series reaches 144 hours. They are raster images a pilot reads for fronts, pressure systems and precipitation shields. This page displays them with their issuing office and valid time and never interprets them: no category, wind, ceiling, ranking or go/no-go here is derived from an image. The prog-chart panel is built for issue #41 item A-4 but KLZU_PROGCHART_ENABLED is off for this run, so no chart was requested. Grey means not enabled here; it never means clear weather.
NOTAM
FAA NOTAM (NMS) — Notices to Air Missions: closures, outages, obstacles and TFRs, issued continuously by the FAA and valid until cancelled. On this page they are advisory evidence about the airport, not weather, and they never change a flight category. The FAA NMS adapter is built but not enabled on this page. Grey means not enabled here; it never means there are no NOTAMs.

A raster chart may be displayed with its issuing office and valid time. No category, wind, ceiling, ranking or go/no-go on this page is derived from, or attributed to, an image. If retrieval fails the slot says UNAVAILABLE; it is never left blank.

Forecast evidence
METAR
METAR — the routine surface observation issued hourly by the reporting station, with SPECI reports off-cycle, carrying ceiling, visibility, wind, temperature and altimeter. Issued by the observing station and distributed by aviationweather.gov. This is measured fact, not a forecast, and on this page it describes conditions right now, not this day. No usable current THIS AIRPORT observation was available this run (state: unavailable). That says nothing about the forecast for this day.
TAF
TAF — the Terminal Aerodrome Forecast, the highest-resolution aviation forecast available. The National Weather Service issues it four times a day, valid 24 to 30 hours, with explicit FM and TEMPO change groups. Airports without their own TAF station use a nearby proxy, which is a normal condition and not a fault. No usable TAF covers the planned dates at this airport (state: unavailable). A TAF reaches only about 30 hours, so a later trip day being uncovered is a horizon fact, not a fault.
MAV
GFS MOS (MAV) — Model Output Statistics, the GFS model bias-corrected against decades of observations at this station. Issued four times a day in three-hourly steps out to about 72 hours. It carries an explicit ceiling and visibility category, so this card uses it to resolve a day the TAF cannot reach. No usable GFS MOS guidance for the planned dates at this airport (state: unavailable). The product reaches about 72 hours.
MEX
GFS extended MOS (MEX) — the extended-range MOS product, issued twice a day in twelve-hourly steps out to about 192 hours. Coarse, but the only station-calibrated numeric guidance that reaches the far end of a long weekend. This card shows it only as a labelled rough outlook and never as a resolved forecast. No usable MEX MOS guidance for the planned dates at this airport (state: unavailable). The product reaches about 192 hours.
GFA
GFA and prog charts — the Graphical Forecast for Aviation and the Weather Prediction Center surface progs, issued by the National Weather Service through the day; the surface prog series reaches 144 hours. They are raster images a pilot reads for fronts, pressure systems and precipitation shields. This page displays them with their issuing office and valid time and never interprets them: no category, wind, ceiling, ranking or go/no-go here is derived from an image. The prog-chart panel is built for issue #41 item A-4 but KLZU_PROGCHART_ENABLED is off for this run, so no chart was requested. Grey means not enabled here; it never means clear weather.
NOTAM
FAA NOTAM (NMS) — Notices to Air Missions: closures, outages, obstacles and TFRs, issued continuously by the FAA and valid until cancelled. On this page they are advisory evidence about the airport, not weather, and they never change a flight category. The FAA NMS adapter is built but not enabled on this page. Grey means not enabled here; it never means there are no NOTAMs.

A raster chart may be displayed with its issuing office and valid time. No category, wind, ceiling, ranking or go/no-go on this page is derived from, or attributed to, an image. If retrieval fails the slot says UNAVAILABLE; it is never left blank.

Forecast evidence
METAR
METAR — the routine surface observation issued hourly by the reporting station, with SPECI reports off-cycle, carrying ceiling, visibility, wind, temperature and altimeter. Issued by the observing station and distributed by aviationweather.gov. This is measured fact, not a forecast, and on this page it describes conditions right now, not this day. No usable current THIS AIRPORT observation was available this run (state: unavailable). That says nothing about the forecast for this day.
TAF
TAF — the Terminal Aerodrome Forecast, the highest-resolution aviation forecast available. The National Weather Service issues it four times a day, valid 24 to 30 hours, with explicit FM and TEMPO change groups. Airports without their own TAF station use a nearby proxy, which is a normal condition and not a fault. No usable TAF covers the planned dates at this airport (state: unavailable). A TAF reaches only about 30 hours, so a later trip day being uncovered is a horizon fact, not a fault.
MAV
GFS MOS (MAV) — Model Output Statistics, the GFS model bias-corrected against decades of observations at this station. Issued four times a day in three-hourly steps out to about 72 hours. It carries an explicit ceiling and visibility category, so this card uses it to resolve a day the TAF cannot reach. No usable GFS MOS guidance for the planned dates at this airport (state: unavailable). The product reaches about 72 hours.
MEX
GFS extended MOS (MEX) — the extended-range MOS product, issued twice a day in twelve-hourly steps out to about 192 hours. Coarse, but the only station-calibrated numeric guidance that reaches the far end of a long weekend. This card shows it only as a labelled rough outlook and never as a resolved forecast. No usable MEX MOS guidance for the planned dates at this airport (state: unavailable). The product reaches about 192 hours.
GFA
GFA and prog charts — the Graphical Forecast for Aviation and the Weather Prediction Center surface progs, issued by the National Weather Service through the day; the surface prog series reaches 144 hours. They are raster images a pilot reads for fronts, pressure systems and precipitation shields. This page displays them with their issuing office and valid time and never interprets them: no category, wind, ceiling, ranking or go/no-go here is derived from an image. The prog-chart panel is built for issue #41 item A-4 but KLZU_PROGCHART_ENABLED is off for this run, so no chart was requested. Grey means not enabled here; it never means clear weather.
NOTAM
FAA NOTAM (NMS) — Notices to Air Missions: closures, outages, obstacles and TFRs, issued continuously by the FAA and valid until cancelled. On this page they are advisory evidence about the airport, not weather, and they never change a flight category. The FAA NMS adapter is built but not enabled on this page. Grey means not enabled here; it never means there are no NOTAMs.

A raster chart may be displayed with its issuing office and valid time. No category, wind, ceiling, ranking or go/no-go on this page is derived from, or attributed to, an image. If retrieval fails the slot says UNAVAILABLE; it is never left blank.

Forecast evidence
METAR
METAR — the routine surface observation issued hourly by the reporting station, with SPECI reports off-cycle, carrying ceiling, visibility, wind, temperature and altimeter. Issued by the observing station and distributed by aviationweather.gov. This is measured fact, not a forecast, and on this page it describes conditions right now, not this day. No usable current THIS AIRPORT observation was available this run (state: unavailable). That says nothing about the forecast for this day.
TAF
TAF — the Terminal Aerodrome Forecast, the highest-resolution aviation forecast available. The National Weather Service issues it four times a day, valid 24 to 30 hours, with explicit FM and TEMPO change groups. Airports without their own TAF station use a nearby proxy, which is a normal condition and not a fault. No usable TAF covers the planned dates at this airport (state: unavailable). A TAF reaches only about 30 hours, so a later trip day being uncovered is a horizon fact, not a fault.
MAV
GFS MOS (MAV) — Model Output Statistics, the GFS model bias-corrected against decades of observations at this station. Issued four times a day in three-hourly steps out to about 72 hours. It carries an explicit ceiling and visibility category, so this card uses it to resolve a day the TAF cannot reach. No usable GFS MOS guidance for the planned dates at this airport (state: unavailable). The product reaches about 72 hours.
MEX
GFS extended MOS (MEX) — the extended-range MOS product, issued twice a day in twelve-hourly steps out to about 192 hours. Coarse, but the only station-calibrated numeric guidance that reaches the far end of a long weekend. This card shows it only as a labelled rough outlook and never as a resolved forecast. No usable MEX MOS guidance for the planned dates at this airport (state: unavailable). The product reaches about 192 hours.
GFA
GFA and prog charts — the Graphical Forecast for Aviation and the Weather Prediction Center surface progs, issued by the National Weather Service through the day; the surface prog series reaches 144 hours. They are raster images a pilot reads for fronts, pressure systems and precipitation shields. This page displays them with their issuing office and valid time and never interprets them: no category, wind, ceiling, ranking or go/no-go here is derived from an image. The prog-chart panel is built for issue #41 item A-4 but KLZU_PROGCHART_ENABLED is off for this run, so no chart was requested. Grey means not enabled here; it never means clear weather.
NOTAM
FAA NOTAM (NMS) — Notices to Air Missions: closures, outages, obstacles and TFRs, issued continuously by the FAA and valid until cancelled. On this page they are advisory evidence about the airport, not weather, and they never change a flight category. The FAA NMS adapter is built but not enabled on this page. Grey means not enabled here; it never means there are no NOTAMs.

A raster chart may be displayed with its issuing office and valid time. No category, wind, ceiling, ranking or go/no-go on this page is derived from, or attributed to, an image. If retrieval fails the slot says UNAVAILABLE; it is never left blank.

Forecast evidence
METAR
METAR — the routine surface observation issued hourly by the reporting station, with SPECI reports off-cycle, carrying ceiling, visibility, wind, temperature and altimeter. Issued by the observing station and distributed by aviationweather.gov. This is measured fact, not a forecast, and on this page it describes conditions right now, not this day. No usable current THIS AIRPORT observation was available this run (state: unavailable). That says nothing about the forecast for this day.
TAF
TAF — the Terminal Aerodrome Forecast, the highest-resolution aviation forecast available. The National Weather Service issues it four times a day, valid 24 to 30 hours, with explicit FM and TEMPO change groups. Airports without their own TAF station use a nearby proxy, which is a normal condition and not a fault. No usable TAF covers the planned dates at this airport (state: unavailable). A TAF reaches only about 30 hours, so a later trip day being uncovered is a horizon fact, not a fault.
MAV
GFS MOS (MAV) — Model Output Statistics, the GFS model bias-corrected against decades of observations at this station. Issued four times a day in three-hourly steps out to about 72 hours. It carries an explicit ceiling and visibility category, so this card uses it to resolve a day the TAF cannot reach. No usable GFS MOS guidance for the planned dates at this airport (state: unavailable). The product reaches about 72 hours.
MEX
GFS extended MOS (MEX) — the extended-range MOS product, issued twice a day in twelve-hourly steps out to about 192 hours. Coarse, but the only station-calibrated numeric guidance that reaches the far end of a long weekend. This card shows it only as a labelled rough outlook and never as a resolved forecast. No usable MEX MOS guidance for the planned dates at this airport (state: unavailable). The product reaches about 192 hours.
GFA
GFA and prog charts — the Graphical Forecast for Aviation and the Weather Prediction Center surface progs, issued by the National Weather Service through the day; the surface prog series reaches 144 hours. They are raster images a pilot reads for fronts, pressure systems and precipitation shields. This page displays them with their issuing office and valid time and never interprets them: no category, wind, ceiling, ranking or go/no-go here is derived from an image. The prog-chart panel is built for issue #41 item A-4 but KLZU_PROGCHART_ENABLED is off for this run, so no chart was requested. Grey means not enabled here; it never means clear weather.
NOTAM
FAA NOTAM (NMS) — Notices to Air Missions: closures, outages, obstacles and TFRs, issued continuously by the FAA and valid until cancelled. On this page they are advisory evidence about the airport, not weather, and they never change a flight category. The FAA NMS adapter is built but not enabled on this page. Grey means not enabled here; it never means there are no NOTAMs.

A raster chart may be displayed with its issuing office and valid time. No category, wind, ceiling, ranking or go/no-go on this page is derived from, or attributed to, an image. If retrieval fails the slot says UNAVAILABLE; it is never left blank.

GFA and prog charts — the Graphical Forecast for Aviation and the Weather Prediction Center surface progs, issued by the National Weather Service through the day; the surface prog series reaches 144 hours. They are raster images a pilot reads for fronts, pressure systems and precipitation shields. This page displays them with their issuing office and valid time and never interprets them: no category, wind, ceiling, ranking or go/no-go here is derived from an image. The prog-chart panel is built for issue #41 item A-4 but KLZU_PROGCHART_ENABLED is off for this run, so no chart was requested. Grey means not enabled here; it never means clear weather.
NOTAM
FAA NOTAM (NMS) — Notices to Air Missions: closures, outages, obstacles and TFRs, issued continuously by the FAA and valid until cancelled. On this page they are advisory evidence about the airport, not weather, and they never change a flight category. The FAA NMS adapter is built but not enabled on this page. Grey means not enabled here; it never means there are no NOTAMs.

A raster chart may be displayed with its issuing office and valid time. No category, wind, ceiling, ranking or go/no-go on this page is derived from, or attributed to, an image. If retrieval fails the slot says UNAVAILABLE; it is never left blank.

Forecast evidence
METAR
METAR — the routine surface observation issued hourly by the reporting station, with SPECI reports off-cycle, carrying ceiling, visibility, wind, temperature and altimeter. Issued by the observing station and distributed by aviationweather.gov. This is measured fact, not a forecast, and on this page it describes conditions right now, not this day. No usable current THIS AIRPORT observation was available this run (state: unavailable). That says nothing about the forecast for this day.
TAF
TAF — the Terminal Aerodrome Forecast, the highest-resolution aviation forecast available. The National Weather Service issues it four times a day, valid 24 to 30 hours, with explicit FM and TEMPO change groups. Airports without their own TAF station use a nearby proxy, which is a normal condition and not a fault. No usable TAF covers the planned dates at this airport (state: unavailable). A TAF reaches only about 30 hours, so a later trip day being uncovered is a horizon fact, not a fault.
MAV
GFS MOS (MAV) — Model Output Statistics, the GFS model bias-corrected against decades of observations at this station. Issued four times a day in three-hourly steps out to about 72 hours. It carries an explicit ceiling and visibility category, so this card uses it to resolve a day the TAF cannot reach. No usable GFS MOS guidance for the planned dates at this airport (state: unavailable). The product reaches about 72 hours.
MEX
GFS extended MOS (MEX) — the extended-range MOS product, issued twice a day in twelve-hourly steps out to about 192 hours. Coarse, but the only station-calibrated numeric guidance that reaches the far end of a long weekend. This card shows it only as a labelled rough outlook and never as a resolved forecast. No usable MEX MOS guidance for the planned dates at this airport (state: unavailable). The product reaches about 192 hours.
GFA
GFA and prog charts — the Graphical Forecast for Aviation and the Weather Prediction Center surface progs, issued by the National Weather Service through the day; the surface prog series reaches 144 hours. They are raster images a pilot reads for fronts, pressure systems and precipitation shields. This page displays them with their issuing office and valid time and never interprets them: no category, wind, ceiling, ranking or go/no-go here is derived from an image. The prog-chart panel is built for issue #41 item A-4 but KLZU_PROGCHART_ENABLED is off for this run, so no chart was requested. Grey means not enabled here; it never means clear weather.
NOTAM
FAA NOTAM (NMS) — Notices to Air Missions: closures, outages, obstacles and TFRs, issued continuously by the FAA and valid until cancelled. On this page they are advisory evidence about the airport, not weather, and they never change a flight category. The FAA NMS adapter is built but not enabled on this page. Grey means not enabled here; it never means there are no NOTAMs.

A raster chart may be displayed with its issuing office and valid time. No category, wind, ceiling, ranking or go/no-go on this page is derived from, or attributed to, an image. If retrieval fails the slot says UNAVAILABLE; it is never left blank.

Forecast evidence
METAR
METAR — the routine surface observation issued hourly by the reporting station, with SPECI reports off-cycle, carrying ceiling, visibility, wind, temperature and altimeter. Issued by the observing station and distributed by aviationweather.gov. This is measured fact, not a forecast, and on this page it describes conditions right now, not this day. No usable current THIS AIRPORT observation was available this run (state: unavailable). That says nothing about the forecast for this day.
TAF
TAF — the Terminal Aerodrome Forecast, the highest-resolution aviation forecast available. The National Weather Service issues it four times a day, valid 24 to 30 hours, with explicit FM and TEMPO change groups. Airports without their own TAF station use a nearby proxy, which is a normal condition and not a fault. No usable TAF covers the planned dates at this airport (state: unavailable). A TAF reaches only about 30 hours, so a later trip day being uncovered is a horizon fact, not a fault.
MAV
GFS MOS (MAV) — Model Output Statistics, the GFS model bias-corrected against decades of observations at this station. Issued four times a day in three-hourly steps out to about 72 hours. It carries an explicit ceiling and visibility category, so this card uses it to resolve a day the TAF cannot reach. No usable GFS MOS guidance for the planned dates at this airport (state: unavailable). The product reaches about 72 hours.
MEX
GFS extended MOS (MEX) — the extended-range MOS product, issued twice a day in twelve-hourly steps out to about 192 hours. Coarse, but the only station-calibrated numeric guidance that reaches the far end of a long weekend. This card shows it only as a labelled rough outlook and never as a resolved forecast. No usable MEX MOS guidance for the planned dates at this airport (state: unavailable). The product reaches about 192 hours.
GFA
GFA and prog charts — the Graphical Forecast for Aviation and the Weather Prediction Center surface progs, issued by the National Weather Service through the day; the surface prog series reaches 144 hours. They are raster images a pilot reads for fronts, pressure systems and precipitation shields. This page displays them with their issuing office and valid time and never interprets them: no category, wind, ceiling, ranking or go/no-go here is derived from an image. The prog-chart panel is built for issue #41 item A-4 but KLZU_PROGCHART_ENABLED is off for this run, so no chart was requested. Grey means not enabled here; it never means clear weather.
NOTAM
FAA NOTAM (NMS) — Notices to Air Missions: closures, outages, obstacles and TFRs, issued continuously by the FAA and valid until cancelled. On this page they are advisory evidence about the airport, not weather, and they never change a flight category. The FAA NMS adapter is built but not enabled on this page. Grey means not enabled here; it never means there are no NOTAMs.

A raster chart may be displayed with its issuing office and valid time. No category, wind, ceiling, ranking or go/no-go on this page is derived from, or attributed to, an image. If retrieval fails the slot says UNAVAILABLE; it is never left blank.

METAR

MEX
GFS extended MOS (MEX) — the extended-range MOS product, issued twice a day in twelve-hourly steps out to about 192 hours. Forecast evidence
METAR
METAR — the routine surface observation issued hourly by the reporting station, with SPECI reports off-cycle, carrying ceiling, visibility, wind, temperature and altimeter. Issued by the observing station and distributed by aviationweather.gov. This is measured fact, not a forecast, and on this page it describes conditions right now, not this day. No usable current THIS AIRPORT observation was available this run (state: unavailable). That says nothing about the forecast for this day.
TAF
TAF — the Terminal Aerodrome Forecast, the highest-resolution aviation forecast available. The National Weather Service issues it four times a day, valid 24 to 30 hours, with explicit FM and TEMPO change groups. Airports without their own TAF station use a nearby proxy, which is a normal condition and not a fault. No usable TAF covers the planned dates at this airport (state: unavailable). A TAF reaches only about 30 hours, so a later trip day being uncovered is a horizon fact, not a fault.
MAV
GFS MOS (MAV) — Model Output Statistics, the GFS model bias-corrected against decades of observations at this station. Issued four times a day in three-hourly steps out to about 72 hours. It carries an explicit ceiling and visibility category, so this card uses it to resolve a day the TAF cannot reach. No usable GFS MOS guidance for the planned dates at this airport (state: unavailable). The product reaches about 72 hours.
MEX
GFS extended MOS (MEX) — the extended-range MOS product, issued twice a day in twelve-hourly steps out to about 192 hours. Coarse, but the only station-calibrated numeric guidance that reaches the far end of a long weekend. This card shows it only as a labelled rough outlook and never as a resolved forecast. No usable MEX MOS guidance for the planned dates at this airport (state: unavailable). The product reaches about 192 hours.
GFA
GFA and prog charts — the Graphical Forecast for Aviation and the Weather Prediction Center surface progs, issued by the National Weather Service through the day; the surface prog series reaches 144 hours. They are raster images a pilot reads for fronts, pressure systems and precipitation shields. This page displays them with their issuing office and valid time and never interprets them: no category, wind, ceiling, ranking or go/no-go here is derived from an image. The prog-chart panel is built for issue #41 item A-4 but KLZU_PROGCHART_ENABLED is off for this run, so no chart was requested. Grey means not enabled here; it never means clear weather.
NOTAM
FAA NOTAM (NMS) — Notices to Air Missions: closures, outages, obstacles and TFRs, issued continuously by the FAA and valid until cancelled. On this page they are advisory evidence about the airport, not weather, and they never change a flight category. The FAA NMS adapter is built but not enabled on this page. Grey means not enabled here; it never means there are no NOTAMs.

A raster chart may be displayed with its issuing office and valid time. No category, wind, ceiling, ranking or go/no-go on this page is derived from, or attributed to, an image. If retrieval fails the slot says UNAVAILABLE; it is never left blank.

Airports without their own TAF station use a nearby proxy, which is a normal condition and not a fault. No usable TAF covers the planned dates at this airport (state: unavailable). A TAF reaches only about 30 hours, so a later trip day being uncovered is a horizon fact, not a fault.
MAV
GFS MOS (MAV) — Model Output Statistics, the GFS model bias-corrected against decades of observations at this station. Issued four times a day in three-hourly steps out to about 72 hours. It carries an explicit ceiling and visibility category, so this card uses it to resolve a day the TAF cannot reach. No usable GFS MOS guidance for the planned dates at this airport (state: unavailable). The product reaches about 72 hours.
MEX
GFS extended MOS (MEX) — the extended-range MOS product, issued twice a day in twelve-hourly steps out to about 192 hours. Coarse, but the only station-calibrated numeric guidance that reaches the far end of a long weekend. This card shows it only as a labelled rough outlook and never as a resolved forecast. No usable MEX MOS guidance for the planned dates at this airport (state: unavailable). The product reaches about 192 hours.
GFA
GFA and prog charts — the Graphical Forecast for Aviation and the Weather Prediction Center surface progs, issued by the National Weather Service through the day; the surface prog series reaches 144 hours. They are raster images a pilot reads for fronts, pressure systems and precipitation shields. This page displays them with their issuing office and valid time and never interprets them: no category, wind, ceiling, ranking or go/no-go here is derived from an image. The prog-chart panel is built for issue #41 item A-4 but KLZU_PROGCHART_ENABLED is off for this run, so no chart was requested. Grey means not enabled here; it never means clear weather.
NOTAM
FAA NOTAM (NMS) — Notices to Air Missions: closures, outages, obstacles and TFRs, issued continuously by the FAA and valid until cancelled. On this page they are advisory evidence about the airport, not weather, and they never change a flight category. The FAA NMS adapter is built but not enabled on this page. Grey means not enabled here; it never means there are no NOTAMs.

A raster chart may be displayed with its issuing office and valid time. No category, wind, ceiling, ranking or go/no-go on this page is derived from, or attributed to, an image. If retrieval fails the slot says UNAVAILABLE; it is never left blank.

Forecast evidence
METAR
METAR — the routine surface observation issued hourly by the reporting station, with SPECI reports off-cycle, carrying ceiling, visibility, wind, temperature and altimeter. Issued by the observing station and distributed by aviationweather.gov. This is measured fact, not a forecast, and on this page it describes conditions right now, not this day. No usable current THIS AIRPORT observation was available this run (state: unavailable). That says nothing about the forecast for this day.
TAF
TAF — the Terminal Aerodrome Forecast, the highest-resolution aviation forecast available. The National Weather Service issues it four times a day, valid 24 to 30 hours, with explicit FM and TEMPO change groups. Airports without their own TAF station use a nearby proxy, which is a normal condition and not a fault. No usable TAF covers the planned dates at this airport (state: unavailable). A TAF reaches only about 30 hours, so a later trip day being uncovered is a horizon fact, not a fault.
MAV
GFS MOS (MAV) — Model Output Statistics, the GFS model bias-corrected against decades of observations at this station. Issued four times a day in three-hourly steps out to about 72 hours. It carries an explicit ceiling and visibility category, so this card uses it to resolve a day the TAF cannot reach. No usable GFS MOS guidance for the planned dates at this airport (state: unavailable). The product reaches about 72 hours.
MEX
GFS extended MOS (MEX) — the extended-range MOS product, issued twice a day in twelve-hourly steps out to about 192 hours. Coarse, but the only station-calibrated numeric guidance that reaches the far end of a long weekend. This card shows it only as a labelled rough outlook and never as a resolved forecast. No usable MEX MOS guidance for the planned dates at this airport (state: unavailable). The product reaches about 192 hours.
GFA
GFA and prog charts — the Graphical Forecast for Aviation and the Weather Prediction Center surface progs, issued by the National Weather Service through the day; the surface prog series reaches 144 hours. They are raster images a pilot reads for fronts, pressure systems and precipitation shields. This page displays them with their issuing office and valid time and never interprets them: no category, wind, ceiling, ranking or go/no-go here is derived from an image. The prog-chart panel is built for issue #41 item A-4 but KLZU_PROGCHART_ENABLED is off for this run, so no chart was requested. Grey means not enabled here; it never means clear weather.
NOTAM
FAA NOTAM (NMS) — Notices to Air Missions: closures, outages, obstacles and TFRs, issued continuously by the FAA and valid until cancelled. On this page they are advisory evidence about the airport, not weather, and they never change a flight category. The FAA NMS adapter is built but not enabled on this page. Grey means not enabled here; it never means there are no NOTAMs.

A raster chart may be displayed with its issuing office and valid time. No category, wind, ceiling, ranking or go/no-go on this page is derived from, or attributed to, an image. If retrieval fails the slot says UNAVAILABLE; it is never left blank.

Forecast evidence
METAR
METAR — the routine surface observation issued hourly by the reporting station, with SPECI reports off-cycle, carrying ceiling, visibility, wind, temperature and altimeter. Issued by the observing station and distributed by aviationweather.gov. This is measured fact, not a forecast, and on this page it describes conditions right now, not this day. No usable current THIS AIRPORT observation was available this run (state: unavailable). That says nothing about the forecast for this day.
TAF
TAF — the Terminal Aerodrome Forecast, the highest-resolution aviation forecast available. The National Weather Service issues it four times a day, valid 24 to 30 hours, with explicit FM and TEMPO change groups. Airports without their own TAF station use a nearby proxy, which is a normal condition and not a fault. No usable TAF covers the planned dates at this airport (state: unavailable). A TAF reaches only about 30 hours, so a later trip day being uncovered is a horizon fact, not a fault.
MAV
GFS MOS (MAV) — Model Output Statistics, the GFS model bias-corrected against decades of observations at this station. Issued four times a day in three-hourly steps out to about 72 hours. It carries an explicit ceiling and visibility category, so this card uses it to resolve a day the TAF cannot reach. No usable GFS MOS guidance for the planned dates at this airport (state: unavailable). The product reaches about 72 hours.
MEX
GFS extended MOS (MEX) — the extended-range MOS product, issued twice a day in twelve-hourly steps out to about 192 hours. Coarse, but the only station-calibrated numeric guidance that reaches the far end of a long weekend. This card shows it only as a labelled rough outlook and never as a resolved forecast. No usable MEX MOS guidance for the planned dates at this airport (state: unavailable). The product reaches about 192 hours.
GFA
GFA and prog charts — the Graphical Forecast for Aviation and the Weather Prediction Center surface progs, issued by the National Weather Service through the day; the surface prog series reaches 144 hours. They are raster images a pilot reads for fronts, pressure systems and precipitation shields. This page displays them with their issuing office and valid time and never interprets them: no category, wind, ceiling, ranking or go/no-go here is derived from an image. The prog-chart panel is built for issue #41 item A-4 but KLZU_PROGCHART_ENABLED is off for this run, so no chart was requested. Grey means not enabled here; it never means clear weather.
NOTAM
FAA NOTAM (NMS) — Notices to Air Missions: closures, outages, obstacles and TFRs, issued continuously by the FAA and valid until cancelled. On this page they are advisory evidence about the airport, not weather, and they never change a flight category. The FAA NMS adapter is built but not enabled on this page. Grey means not enabled here; it never means there are no NOTAMs.

A raster chart may be displayed with its issuing office and valid time. No category, wind, ceiling, ranking or go/no-go on this page is derived from, or attributed to, an image. If retrieval fails the slot says UNAVAILABLE; it is never left blank.

Forecast evidence
METAR
METAR — the routine surface observation issued hourly by the reporting station, with SPECI reports off-cycle, carrying ceiling, visibility, wind, temperature and altimeter. Issued by the observing station and distributed by aviationweather.gov. This is measured fact, not a forecast, and on this page it describes conditions right now, not this day. No usable current THIS AIRPORT observation was available this run (state: unavailable). That says nothing about the forecast for this day.
TAF
TAF — the Terminal Aerodrome Forecast, the highest-resolution aviation forecast available. The National Weather Service issues it four times a day, valid 24 to 30 hours, with explicit FM and TEMPO change groups. Airports without their own TAF station use a nearby proxy, which is a normal condition and not a fault. No usable TAF covers the planned dates at this airport (state: unavailable). A TAF reaches only about 30 hours, so a later trip day being uncovered is a horizon fact, not a fault.
MAV
GFS MOS (MAV) — Model Output Statistics, the GFS model bias-corrected against decades of observations at this station. Issued four times a day in three-hourly steps out to about 72 hours. It carries an explicit ceiling and visibility category, so this card uses it to resolve a day the TAF cannot reach. No usable GFS MOS guidance for the planned dates at this airport (state: unavailable). The product reaches about 72 hours.
MEX
GFS extended MOS (MEX) — the extended-range MOS product, issued twice a day in twelve-hourly steps out to about 192 hours. Coarse, but the only station-calibrated numeric guidance that reaches the far end of a long weekend. This card shows it only as a labelled rough outlook and never as a resolved forecast. No usable MEX MOS guidance for the planned dates at this airport (state: unavailable). The product reaches about 192 hours.
GFA
GFA and prog charts — the Graphical Forecast for Aviation and the Weather Prediction Center surface progs, issued by the National Weather Service through the day; the surface prog series reaches 144 hours. They are raster images a pilot reads for fronts, pressure systems and precipitation shields. This page displays them with their issuing office and valid time and never interprets them: no category, wind, ceiling, ranking or go/no-go here is derived from an image. The prog-chart panel is built for issue #41 item A-4 but KLZU_PROGCHART_ENABLED is off for this run, so no chart was requested. Grey means not enabled here; it never means clear weather.
NOTAM
FAA NOTAM (NMS) — Notices to Air Missions: closures, outages, obstacles and TFRs, issued continuously by the FAA and valid until cancelled. On this page they are advisory evidence about the airport, not weather, and they never change a flight category. The FAA NMS adapter is built but not enabled on this page. Grey means not enabled here; it never means there are no NOTAMs.

A raster chart may be displayed with its issuing office and valid time. No category, wind, ceiling, ranking or go/no-go on this page is derived from, or attributed to, an image. If retrieval fails the slot says UNAVAILABLE; it is never left blank.

Forecast evidence
METAR
METAR — the routine surface observation issued hourly by the reporting station, with SPECI reports off-cycle, carrying ceiling, visibility, wind, temperature and altimeter. Issued by the observing station and distributed by aviationweather.gov. This is measured fact, not a forecast, and on this page it describes conditions right now, not this day. No usable current THIS AIRPORT observation was available this run (state: unavailable). That says nothing about the forecast for this day.
TAF
TAF — the Terminal Aerodrome Forecast, the highest-resolution aviation forecast available. The National Weather Service issues it four times a day, valid 24 to 30 hours, with explicit FM and TEMPO change groups. Airports without their own TAF station use a nearby proxy, which is a normal condition and not a fault. No usable TAF covers the planned dates at this airport (state: unavailable). A TAF reaches only about 30 hours, so a later trip day being uncovered is a horizon fact, not a fault.
MAV
GFS MOS (MAV) — Model Output Statistics, the GFS model bias-corrected against decades of observations at this station. Issued four times a day in three-hourly steps out to about 72 hours. It carries an explicit ceiling and visibility category, so this card uses it to resolve a day the TAF cannot reach. No usable GFS MOS guidance for the planned dates at this airport (state: unavailable). The product reaches about 72 hours.
MEX
GFS extended MOS (MEX) — the extended-range MOS product, issued twice a day in twelve-hourly steps out to about 192 hours. Coarse, but the only station-calibrated numeric guidance that reaches the far end of a long weekend. This card shows it only as a labelled rough outlook and never as a resolved forecast. No usable MEX MOS guidance for the planned dates at this airport (state: unavailable). The product reaches about 192 hours.
GFA
GFA and prog charts — the Graphical Forecast for Aviation and the Weather Prediction Center surface progs, issued by the National Weather Service through the day; the surface prog series reaches 144 hours. They are raster images a pilot reads for fronts, pressure systems and precipitation shields. This page displays them with their issuing office and valid time and never interprets them: no category, wind, ceiling, ranking or go/no-go here is derived from an image. The prog-chart panel is built for issue #41 item A-4 but KLZU_PROGCHART_ENABLED is off for this run, so no chart was requested. Grey means not enabled here; it never means clear weather.
NOTAM
FAA NOTAM (NMS) — Notices to Air Missions: closures, outages, obstacles and TFRs, issued continuously by the FAA and valid until cancelled. On this page they are advisory evidence about the airport, not weather, and they never change a flight category. The FAA NMS adapter is built but not enabled on this page. Grey means not enabled here; it never means there are no NOTAMs.

A raster chart may be displayed with its issuing office and valid time. No category, wind, ceiling, ranking or go/no-go on this page is derived from, or attributed to, an image. If retrieval fails the slot says UNAVAILABLE; it is never left blank.

Forecast evidence
METAR
METAR — the routine surface observation issued hourly by the reporting station, with SPECI reports off-cycle, carrying ceiling, visibility, wind, temperature and altimeter. Issued by the observing station and distributed by aviationweather.gov. This is measured fact, not a forecast, and on this page it describes conditions right now, not this day. No usable current THIS AIRPORT observation was available this run (state: unavailable). That says nothing about the forecast for this day.
TAF
TAF — the Terminal Aerodrome Forecast, the highest-resolution aviation forecast available. The National Weather Service issues it four times a day, valid 24 to 30 hours, with explicit FM and TEMPO change groups. Airports without their own TAF station use a nearby proxy, which is a normal condition and not a fault. No usable TAF covers the planned dates at this airport (state: unavailable). A TAF reaches only about 30 hours, so a later trip day being uncovered is a horizon fact, not a fault.
MAV
GFS MOS (MAV) — Model Output Statistics, the GFS model bias-corrected against decades of observations at this station. Issued four times a day in three-hourly steps out to about 72 hours. It carries an explicit ceiling and visibility category, so this card uses it to resolve a day the TAF cannot reach. No usable GFS MOS guidance for the planned dates at this airport (state: unavailable). The product reaches about 72 hours.
MEX
GFS extended MOS (MEX) — the extended-range MOS product, issued twice a day in twelve-hourly steps out to about 192 hours. Coarse, but the only station-calibrated numeric guidance that reaches the far end of a long weekend. This card shows it only as a labelled rough outlook and never as a resolved forecast. No usable MEX MOS guidance for the planned dates at this airport (state: unavailable). The product reaches about 192 hours.
GFA
GFA and prog charts — the Graphical Forecast for Aviation and the Weather Prediction Center surface progs, issued by the National Weather Service through the day; the surface prog series reaches 144 hours. They are raster images a pilot reads for fronts, pressure systems and precipitation shields. This page displays them with their issuing office and valid time and never interprets them: no category, wind, ceiling, ranking or go/no-go here is derived from an image. The prog-chart panel is built for issue #41 item A-4 but KLZU_PROGCHART_ENABLED is off for this run, so no chart was requested. Grey means not enabled here; it never means clear weather.
NOTAM
FAA NOTAM (NMS) — Notices to Air Missions: closures, outages, obstacles and TFRs, issued continuously by the FAA and valid until cancelled. On this page they are advisory evidence about the airport, not weather, and they never change a flight category. The FAA NMS adapter is built but not enabled on this page. Grey means not enabled here; it never means there are no NOTAMs.

A raster chart may be displayed with its issuing office and valid time. No category, wind, ceiling, ranking or go/no-go on this page is derived from, or attributed to, an image. If retrieval fails the slot says UNAVAILABLE; it is never left blank.

Forecast evidence
METAR
METAR — the routine surface observation issued hourly by the reporting station, with SPECI reports off-cycle, carrying ceiling, visibility, wind, temperature and altimeter. Issued by the observing station and distributed by aviationweather.gov. This is measured fact, not a forecast, and on this page it describes conditions right now, not this day. No usable current THIS AIRPORT observation was available this run (state: unavailable). That says nothing about the forecast for this day.
TAF
TAF — the Terminal Aerodrome Forecast, the highest-resolution aviation forecast available. The National Weather Service issues it four times a day, valid 24 to 30 hours, with explicit FM and TEMPO change groups. Airports without their own TAF station use a nearby proxy, which is a normal condition and not a fault. No usable TAF covers the planned dates at this airport (state: unavailable). A TAF reaches only about 30 hours, so a later trip day being uncovered is a horizon fact, not a fault.
MAV
GFS MOS (MAV) — Model Output Statistics, the GFS model bias-corrected against decades of observations at this station. Issued four times a day in three-hourly steps out to about 72 hours. It carries an explicit ceiling and visibility category, so this card uses it to resolve a day the TAF cannot reach. No usable GFS MOS guidance for the planned dates at this airport (state: unavailable). The product reaches about 72 hours.
MEX
GFS extended MOS (MEX) — the extended-range MOS product, issued twice a day in twelve-hourly steps out to about 192 hours. Coarse, but the only station-calibrated numeric guidance that reaches the far end of a long weekend. This card shows it only as a labelled rough outlook and never as a resolved forecast. No usable MEX MOS guidance for the planned dates at this airport (state: unavailable). The product reaches about 192 hours.
GFA
GFA and prog charts — the Graphical Forecast for Aviation and the Weather Prediction Center surface progs, issued by the National Weather Service through the day; the surface prog series reaches 144 hours. They are raster images a pilot reads for fronts, pressure systems and precipitation shields. This page displays them with their issuing office and valid time and never interprets them: no category, wind, ceiling, ranking or go/no-go here is derived from an image. The prog-chart panel is built for issue #41 item A-4 but KLZU_PROGCHART_ENABLED is off for this run, so no chart was requested. Grey means not enabled here; it never means clear weather.
NOTAM
FAA NOTAM (NMS) — Notices to Air Missions: closures, outages, obstacles and TFRs, issued continuously by the FAA and valid until cancelled. On this page they are advisory evidence about the airport, not weather, and they never change a flight category. The FAA NMS adapter is built but not enabled on this page. Grey means not enabled here; it never means there are no NOTAMs.

A raster chart may be displayed with its issuing office and valid time. No category, wind, ceiling, ranking or go/no-go on this page is derived from, or attributed to, an image. If retrieval fails the slot says UNAVAILABLE; it is never left blank.

Forecast evidence
METAR
METAR — the routine surface observation issued hourly by the reporting station, with SPECI reports off-cycle, carrying ceiling, visibility, wind, temperature and altimeter. Issued by the observing station and distributed by aviationweather.gov. This is measured fact, not a forecast, and on this page it describes conditions right now, not this day. No usable current THIS AIRPORT observation was available this run (state: unavailable). That says nothing about the forecast for this day.
TAF
TAF — the Terminal Aerodrome Forecast, the highest-resolution aviation forecast available. The National Weather Service issues it four times a day, valid 24 to 30 hours, with explicit FM and TEMPO change groups. Airports without their own TAF station use a nearby proxy, which is a normal condition and not a fault. No usable TAF covers the planned dates at this airport (state: unavailable). A TAF reaches only about 30 hours, so a later trip day being uncovered is a horizon fact, not a fault.
MAV
GFS MOS (MAV) — Model Output Statistics, the GFS model bias-corrected against decades of observations at this station. Issued four times a day in three-hourly steps out to about 72 hours. It carries an explicit ceiling and visibility category, so this card uses it to resolve a day the TAF cannot reach. No usable GFS MOS guidance for the planned dates at this airport (state: unavailable). The product reaches about 72 hours.
MEX
GFS extended MOS (MEX) — the extended-range MOS product, issued twice a day in twelve-hourly steps out to about 192 hours. Coarse, but the only station-calibrated numeric guidance that reaches the far end of a long weekend. This card shows it only as a labelled rough outlook and never as a resolved forecast. No usable MEX MOS guidance for the planned dates at this airport (state: unavailable). The product reaches about 192 hours.
GFA
GFA and prog charts — the Graphical Forecast for Aviation and the Weather Prediction Center surface progs, issued by the National Weather Service through the day; the surface prog series reaches 144 hours. They are raster images a pilot reads for fronts, pressure systems and precipitation shields. This page displays them with their issuing office and valid time and never interprets them: no category, wind, ceiling, ranking or go/no-go here is derived from an image. The prog-chart panel is built for issue #41 item A-4 but KLZU_PROGCHART_ENABLED is off for this run, so no chart was requested. Grey means not enabled here; it never means clear weather.
NOTAM
FAA NOTAM (NMS) — Notices to Air Missions: closures, outages, obstacles and TFRs, issued continuously by the FAA and valid until cancelled. On this page they are advisory evidence about the airport, not weather, and they never change a flight category. The FAA NMS adapter is built but not enabled on this page. Grey means not enabled here; it never means there are no NOTAMs.

A raster chart may be displayed with its issuing office and valid time. No category, wind, ceiling, ranking or go/no-go on this page is derived from, or attributed to, an image. If retrieval fails the slot says UNAVAILABLE; it is never left blank.

METAR
METAR — the routine surface observation issued hourly by the reporting station, with SPECI reports off-cycle, carrying ceiling, visibility, wind, temperature and altimeter. TAF
TAF — the Terminal Aerodrome Forecast, the highest-resolution aviation forecast available. The National Weather Service issues it four times a day, valid 24 to 30 hours, with explicit FM and TEMPO change groups. Airports without their own TAF station use a nearby proxy, which is a normal condition and not a fault. No usable TAF covers the planned dates at this airport (state: unavailable). A TAF reaches only about 30 hours, so a later trip day being uncovered is a horizon fact, not a fault.

GFS MOS (MAV) — Model Output Statistics, the GFS model bias-corrected against decades of observations at this station. Issued four times a day in three-hourly steps out to about 72 hours. It carries an explicit ceiling and visibility category, so this card uses it to resolve a day the TAF cannot reach. No usable GFS MOS guidance for the planned dates at this airport (state: unavailable). The product reaches about 72 hours.
MEX
GFS extended MOS (MEX) — the extended-range MOS product, issued twice a day in twelve-hourly steps out to about 192 hours. Coarse, but the only station-calibrated numeric guidance that reaches the far end of a long weekend. This card shows it only as a labelled rough outlook and never as a resolved forecast. No usable MEX MOS guidance for the planned dates at this airport (state: unavailable). The product reaches about 192 hours.
GFA
GFA and prog charts — the Graphical Forecast for Aviation and the Weather Prediction Center surface progs, issued by the National Weather Service through the day; the surface prog series reaches 144 hours. This page displays them with their issuing office and valid time and never interprets them: no category, wind, ceiling, ranking or go/no-go here is derived from an image. The prog-chart panel is built for issue #41 item A-4 but KLZU_PROGCHART_ENABLED is off for this run, so no chart was requested. Grey means not enabled here; it never means clear weather.
NOTAM
FAA NOTAM (NMS) — Notices to Air Missions: closures, outages, obstacles and TFRs, issued continuously by the FAA and valid until cancelled. On this page they are advisory evidence about the airport, not weather, and they never change a flight category. The FAA NMS adapter is built but not enabled on this page. 3 · Hazard feeds & regional observations

Scope: Hazard counts are raw feed totals and have not been filtered against a proposed route, altitude, or time. Airport flight categories are current point observations, not corridor forecasts.

4 · Planning gates

  • Evidence gate: an unavailable, stale, or out-of-horizon source is unknown — never treat it as favorable.
  • Weather gate: compare current observations and valid-period forecasts with personal ceiling, visibility, convection, wind, and crosswind minimums.
  • Route gate: screen the actual route, altitude, and time against official hazard products; feed totals on this page are not route-filtered.
  • Operations gate: verify NOTAMs, TFRs, runway conditions, fuel, aircraft performance, daylight, and alternates.

5 · ForeFlight manual cross-check (before flight)

  • Official briefing matches these go/no-go windows
  • Prog charts / radar / satellite trend agrees with convection timing
  • Winds & temps aloft along actual route (may shift ETE)
  • NOTAMs & TFRs — airport-scoped NMS records may be shown, but route-wide/TFR coverage is not included; pull a fresh official briefing for departure, destination, and alternates
  • Runway condition / length / closures at destination & alternate
  • Weight & balance + performance at forecast density altitude (heat!)
  • File & brief in ForeFlight; confirm fuel stops if long-range

Executive summaryDeterministic · restates page evidence · no model called

A plain restatement of evidence shown in full below, computed from that evidence with no model call. It reports what the sources say; it does not rank the days, rate them, or make a go/no-go call. It follows the order the owner asked for: feasibility evidence, KLZU, destinations, weather by area or region, then new KLZU NOTAMs.

1 · Feasibility evidence for the trip window

This part is a derivation, not an observation: it states how much of the trip window carries a forecast flight category, and nothing more. It is not a go/no-go call, not a recommendation, and not a flight category. Its inputs and its gaps are listed in the tooltip on the line below.

  • Trip window: Fri Jul 24 - Mon Jul 27, 2026. “This weekend” is taken to mean exactly this window; no other date range is assessed.
  • Trip-window feasibility evidence (Derived): assessable for every active trip day — 4 of 4 active trip days in Fri Jul 24 - Mon Jul 27, 2026 carry a forecast flight category and 0 carry none. This is a derived statement about how much evidence exists, it is not a flight category, and it says nothing about whether a flight is advisable. Every input and every gap is named in this line's tooltip.

2 · KLZU home-base status

The KLZU observation and the per-day board categories, taken from the same helpers the board itself renders from, so the two cannot disagree.

  • KLZU current observation: VFR — from the surface observation read this run; it describes conditions now, not a trip day.
  • Fri Jul 24, 06:00–22:00 ET: MVFR — most restrictive forecast flight category; medium-low confidence; from TAF.

3 · Destination coverage

Coverage, not a pick: this counts which destinations a product permitted to state a flight category actually reaches. It is not a ranking, not a recommendation, and the editorial order of the destination list is not a flyability score.

  • Destinations: 0 of 0 covered airports resolve a forecast flight category on at least one active trip day; 0 resolve none at this lead time. Counted from the same per-day outlook the destination cards render, with outlook-grade blocks excluded.
  • No covered airport resolves a forecast flight category on an active trip day in this run, so no per-airport category is listed. That is the honest answer at this lead time, not a statement that the airports are unusable.
  • NOTAMs: no destination of 0 reports an active NOTAM this run. KLZU departure NOTAM state: UNAVAILABLE.

4 · Weather events by area or region

Weather events by area or region, from products that carry an area. Per-airport categories are never clustered into a region here: an area inferred that way would be a spatial claim no source made.

  • No region-scoped hazard product is available in this run: the SIGMET, G-AIRMET and CWA feeds are read as record counts only, and no polygon, bounding box, FIR or area name is retained, so no geographic extent can be stated. Nothing on this page infers an area from per-airport categories.
  • Hazard feed record counts this run, unfiltered and national: SIGMET 0, G-AIRMET 0, CWA 0; overall feed state unavailable. These are totals over the whole feed, not a count near KLZU, not a count along any route, and not a route assessment.

5 · New KLZU NOTAMs

This run keeps no snapshot of the previous run, so “new” cannot mean “changed since last time”. It is defined below as an FAA-published timestamp window, and the service-status scan reads the published text of every KLZU record so a status embedded inside a record of another category is not missed.

  • Baseline for “new”: a KLZU NOTAM whose own FAA-published timestamp (last update, else issue, else effective start) falls within the 72 hours before this run's generation time (2026-07-20T18:00:00+00:00). This run holds no copy of the previous run's NOTAM set, so this is a source-timestamp window and not a difference against an earlier run.
  • KLZU NOTAM query state is UNAVAILABLE, so this run does not know the KLZU NOTAM picture. No new NOTAM count is stated: an incomplete query is not the same as no NOTAMs.

This restates evidence; it is not a recommendation, not an all-clear, and not a data outage. The decision surfaces are the planning gates and the ForeFlight cross-check below, read against the KLZU board and destination cards. Every line above restates a value shown elsewhere on this page.

Static, dependency-free schematic. No map tiles or network requests are used.

    Features

    What's new (newest first, by merge date)

    • Planner-first navigation restored Aug 23, 2026
      The compact Planner opens by default again, while Mission Control remains available as a separate view without displacing the flight-planning board.
      Use the Planner and Mission Control tabs at the top of the page; printing always uses the Planner.
    • Mission Control destination map Aug 23, 2026
      Mission Control now compares all configured airports on a no-tile schematic map with Trip Pair and Day Scan views, category ranges, filters, clustering, zoom, and synchronized details.
      Choose a destination and dates, then focus or select a marker or matching list row to inspect its four evidence blocks.
    • FAA NMS source decision shown consistently Aug 9, 2026
      NOTAM and Data Health views now identify the unchanged configured FAA NMS feed as the owner-approved production source while retaining its limited evidence scope.
      Read the FAA NMS source pill for the decision label and hover or focus it for technical provenance and the dated 3-of-30-airport spot-check scope.
    • Runway and wind picture on every destination Jul 29, 2026
      Each destination now draws a small schematic of its runways with an arrow for the wind and the wind-favoured end highlighted, so the alignment is visible at a glance.
      Look for "Wind vs runways" on a destination card.
    • Thunderstorm and shower chance on the four-day board Jul 28, 2026
      Forecast change windows now carry a labelled thunderstorm or shower chance, so a day still too far out for a flight-category call no longer goes silent about convection.
      Look for the storm or shower chip in the forecast change windows on the 4-day board.

    Everything the page does

    • Mission Control with destination and day selection, fail-closed category ranges, a keyboard- and touch-operable schematic airport map, filters, clustering, and a synchronized text list
    • Per-source state, validity horizon, and target-date coverage for every destination
    • Explicit unavailable/out-of-horizon target cells; no static weather fallback
    • Per-airport expandable detail — current observations, covered forecasts, dep/dest METAR temperatures
    • Current-and-future KLZU board with four fixed 06:00–22:00 ET boxes and outbound/return day context
    • Source-labelled TAF/MOS flight-category guidance only when a source interval actually covers the visible standard box — a box with no covering interval shows an explicit unavailable/out-of-horizon state instead of a category, never an implied one
    • Timed NWS weather, wind-favored runway (magnetic, from each airport's own runways), gust, and material crosswind context wherever the forecast supplies them
    • Raw METAR/TAF + data-sources dropdown per airport
    • FAA Airport Status & Delays with known, unsupported, and unavailable states
    • Best-effort 100LL fuel prices
    • Auto-refreshed about 4x a day by an hourly scheduler that republishes once 6 h have passed since the last publish, so refresh times drift; the last-updated stamp is exact and the next-run stamp is an estimate
    • Quick links (Flight Circle, ForeFlight, FlightAware) + Feedback
    • FAA chart-cycle stamp (current VFR Sectional + Chart Supplement)
    • Published PDF download plus browser print fallback — print-ready, color-preserving (semantic colors kept on paper)
    • Deterministic evidence-backed page; external AI aviation prose is withheld pending a validated evidence schema, so the executive-summary region shows an explicit pending-feature placeholder instead of generated text
    • Model-labeled MOS target-window outlook per airport (Iowa State GFS with conditional GFS Extended/MEX), with runtime and validity horizon shown
    • Expandable NWS FFC pattern summary and extended outlook inside the KLZU board
    • Per-airport chart links: SkyVector & AirNav/Chart Supplement (deep links)
    • FAA NMS NOTAM adapter with explicit per-airport source states; reporting an explicit error state rather than an empty list, and never a substitute for an official briefing
    • Full run archive: run_manifest.json with all data + provenance log

    Have an idea or found a problem? Use the Feedback button — it opens an issue on the public site repository.
